title: Government Readies Hindustan Zinc Stake Sale to Raise Rs 5,000 Crore in Disinvestment Push
excerpt: The Centre plans to sell up to 2% of its holding in India's largest zinc producer through an offer for sale, building on a renewed drive to meet fiscal targets.
body:
• India's government is planning to sell up to 2% of its ~28% stake in Hindustan Zinc through an offer for sale (OFS), aiming to raise approximately Rs 5,000 crore ($525 million).
  • ICICI Securities, Axis Capital, IIFL Capital Services, and HDFC Securities are advising the government on the transaction.
  • The sale is part of a broader disinvestment push that has already included stake sales in Coal India ($531 million), NHPC ($450 million), and a planned LIC offering worth up to Rs 10,000 crore.
  • Hindustan Zinc shares have gained about 24% since the government's last OFS in November 2024, when it sold 1.6% at Rs 505 per share.

The Sale Plan

The Indian government is preparing another stake sale in Hindustan Zinc Ltd (HZL), with the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) aiming to raise up to Rs 5,000 crore ($525 million) by selling approximately 2% of its holding, according to multiple reports citing people familiar with the matter.

The sale would be conducted through an offer for sale (OFS) on the stock exchanges, the standard mechanism the government has used for minority disinvestment. Four merchant bankers — ICICI Securities, Axis Capital, IIFL Capital Services, and HDFC Securities — are advising on the transaction, sources told Bloomberg.

As of March 31, 2026, the central government held approximately 27.92% of Hindustan Zinc, making it the largest minority shareholder. Vedanta Ltd, controlled by mining billionaire Anil Agarwal, holds approximately 60.71% as the majority promoter.

Part of a Bigger Disinvestment Drive

The HZL stake sale comes as the government has stepped up efforts to raise revenue through disinvestment. In recent months, the Centre has raised about $531 million from a 2% stake sale in Coal India and $450 million from a 6% offering in NHPC. A potential 2% stake sale in Life Insurance Corporation of India could raise as much as Rs 10,000 crore ($1 billion), reports have indicated.

These transactions form part of the government's broader fiscal strategy to meet its disinvestment targets for FY27 while the stock market remains supportive. The Hindustan Zinc holding has become increasingly valuable — the stock has risen approximately 24% since the last OFS in November 2024, when the government sold a 1.6% stake at Rs 505 per share, raising Rs 3,449 crore.

"Selling the entire stake now could fetch around Rs 40,000 crore but would mean forgoing steady future dividends."

— Senior government official, to Moneycontrol

The Dividend Dilemma

The timing of the sale reflects a delicate balancing act. HZL is one of India's most reliable dividend-paying companies, having declared its first interim dividend for FY26 at Rs 10 per share in June. With a dividend yield of approximately 4%, the government's ~28% stake generates substantial recurring income.

The company posted its highest-ever quarterly net profit of Rs 3,003 crore in Q4 FY25, up 47% year-on-year, with revenue of Rs 9,087 crore and an EBITDA margin of 53%. Hindustan Zinc also achieved record mined and refined metal output in FY25, cementing its position as the world's largest integrated zinc producer.

Some officials have favored a staggered approach to disinvestment rather than a large one-time sale, balancing the need for immediate revenue against long-term dividend income. A Moneycontrol report cited a senior official saying the Centre may consider a qualified institutional placement (QIP) as an alternative to OFS.

Market Impact and What's Next

Hindustan Zinc shares were trading at Rs 561.90, down about 2.8% from the previous close. The stock has historically seen selling pressure ahead of OFS announcements, as markets anticipate the discounted floor price that accompanies such offerings. In the November 2024 OFS, shares dropped more than 7% on the day the sale opened.

The floor price for the upcoming OFS has not been announced, but the government typically sets it at an 8-10% discount to the prevailing market price. Institutional investors generally participate on the first day, with retail investors getting a chance on the second day with a 10% reservation of the total offer size.

The government's long-term strategy for its HZL holding remains a question mark. The Supreme Court approved the government's plan to divest its remaining stake through public market channels in 2021. A complete exit at current prices would fetch approximately Rs 40,000 crore, but the staggered approach suggests the government is content to monetize gradually while collecting dividends.
nri_angle: The HZL stake sale offers a window into India's evolving approach to public sector disinvestment and opportunities NRI investors in Indian equities should watch.
